cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Basically Finished
cards.instruction: Describe incomplete, late, or improvised work as a thoughtful version of completion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Your cupboard's finished. I've left the shelves loose so you can choose the heights.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They fall down. You haven't fitted the supports.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. It's complete as an adjustable kit. Position everything around your tins.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I paid you to install it. Here's the drill.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll fasten one shelf at your chosen height. A finished sample, so you can approve the rest.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 declares completion and decision power, A3 delays questions, but A5 shifts approval to the customer without clearly retaining the highest-status ruling.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 missing supports causes A3 kit label; B4 payment and drill cause A5 one-shelf sample, after an unresponsive restriction.

relationship.evidence: B2 reports unusable shelves and B4 asserts the paid scope with a tool, plausibly pressing for the actual work.

heightening.evidence: B4 demand for installation becomes A5 a small completed sample presented as enough for further approval.

specificity.evidence: A1 cupboard and B2 falling shelves establish the incompleteness; B4 payment states the duty.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 finished-sample label is earned by the offered drill, but A3 stock question ban interrupts the redefinition.
